A macaron ice cream sandwich with a Fluff It marshmallow on top? Yes please! There are so many options too, including some very unique ones such as Fruity Pebbles macarons and Netflix and Chill ice cream. The cookie cup consists of two large macarons of your choice (They had strawberry, vanilla, Fruity Pebbles, and red velvet when I was here), four scoops of ice cream, with a marshmallow that is bruleed with a torch in front of you. We got ours with Fruity Pebbles and red velvet macarons, blueberry muffin and white chocolate raspberry ice cream. The entire cup was a beautiful sugary sight to behold. We dug in with gusto. I loved the chewy texture of the macaron with the creamy smooth ice cream and fluffy pillowy marshmallow with caramelized crust. We were definitely satisfied and full after sharing it. The cost was $6.25 pre-tax. Service was very friendly and warm and everyone seemed very happy to be working here. I would be too if I were surrounded with all this delicious bounty! The location is definitely a bit odd as it's hidden in the back of a shopping plaza right next to a residential area. Thanks to Yelp though we were able to indulge in a unique and tasty collaborative dessert we probably wouldn't have been able to see from the street. I'll definitely be back again for more delicious dessert.
Walk up ice cream window. Best ice cream I've had since moving to Las Vegas. They have SOOOOO many flavors. There is usually a line but it is worth it. Make sure you try chocolate cake batter!

DONUT have one!!! LOL. Amazing donuts. The crime brÃ»lÃ©e donuts are so fun to crack open, but my fave was the red velvet donut. Worth the Ã¼ber ride to get there. My 2 wishes... Closer to the strip and if they deliver to California.

Melt is a great place to go for decent ice cream and unique flavors! They got rid of their six flavor sampler, but you really can't go wrong here. Their horchata flavor was amazing and I haven't had a bad cereal flavor yet. With that said, the comments about there being pieces of ice crystals in the ice cream are accurate. Sure, it doesn't compromise the flavor, but it does show it's not the best made ice cream in town. Also, I don't really get the novelty of the ice cream coming in Chinese take-out boxes, but some people really get a kick out of it. Lastly, street parking can be rough to find some nights (but hey, it is downtown Phoenix so what do you expect). This place is definitely worth checking out because of the unique flavors and convenience, but Melt and Mary Coles are close to downtown too and they might be better!

In A Nutshell: -If you are looking for nice sweet, cold sweet treat, then Sweet Republic has it covered. -Their sundaes are plentiful, but if you are there on a Friday, Saturday or Sunday, I suggest you order their "Toffee Banofi". -This sundae features 2 scoops of Madagascar vanilla ice cream, fresh bananas, almond toffee brittle & salted butter caramel sauce in a waffle bowl. -It's big enough to share for two. -Take it outside in the warm night air to enjoy. Overall, this is an award winning ice cream shop located in Scottsdale!

I live in AZ but will be stopping here every time I'm in Vegas which I'd A LOT. Got 3 donuts and couldn't believe how cheap these huge delicious things are. Can not wait to go back and take everyone I know.

Hard to find, tough to beat. Same great flavors and service as the 16th Street location, but without the crowds. There are 2 customer parking spaces on the street level, then a big parking structure. Don't know if the structure parking is free or not.

We went on a campus tour, they gave us coupons for the Daily Scoop, we went for ice cream. So we paid attention when we got there (before the tour) and learned quickly that the line gets backed up fast. When our tour was over, we belined it to the Daily Scoop and orders some ice cream - chocolate peanut butter to be specific. It was good.

The line was long to get in this place and it surely did not disappoint. We picked up mini chocolate mouse cake, red velvet cupcake, cannoli, lobster tail and some kind of cookie bar. Everything was awesome and so fresh! This place is a must try when you're in Vegas!

I heard so much about this place, I had such high expectations... I ordered a chocolate cereal milk (milkshake) and it literally tasted like baby food, I couldn't eat it anymore... I had to throw it away. I felt like the people working there didn't know what they were doing. The place is overrated and overpriced, not worth it.
Good donuts,bring back the donut cake for special occasions if you can! They were delicious!

Ooh, Sweet Republic! I've read so many good things about their ice cream and the bar was set pretty high! We're walking around First Friday when we saw their groovy tangerine van. My hubby got the Belgian Chocolate and my little guy couldn't resist the Butter Caramel. "This is so good!", he exclaimed. White Rose intrigued me. I love the smooth and creamy consistency with a touch of rose syrup. It's worth the $3 for one scoop!
I had the Seacliff it was really good just that I had to literally dig my way to get to the cookie in it.
The butter pecan ice cream is heavenly and the waffle cones were amazing. I would definitely recommend this place for great ice cream.

My son and I stopped in this late evening for a sweet treat after attending the Phoenix Symphony. I checked Yelp for nearby places and stumbled on Novel. We both agreed to give it a try and sure glad we did! There was a short line which extended out the door, but once we got inside it smelled like heaven. You can see all the fresh donuts and the gentleman that helped us (sorry, can't remember his name!) offered us samples of anything we'd like to try. While making our requests he made small talk with us which was nice! Asked our names and how we heard of Novel. We went outside to enjoy our treats where they have several places to sit down. We'll be back again! Parking sucks, but it's downtown Phoenix so it comes with the territory.
Best macaroons EVER. Love this place. Haven't been back since the management changed a while back but it is still my favorite for it's lavender macaroons. Ps. Will have to pop by one of these days.

I have been wanting to try Milk Bar for so long because I heard great things about it. Finally got the chance to try it and I am sadly not in love with it as I want to be. First the service was not the best and the person ringing us up seemed annoyed. I got the birthday cake soft serve and I thought it was okay. Flavor of birthday cake was there but it was overly sweet for me. Also without toppings it was already $6.50. I get that we are on the strip so prices tend be higher. My husband got the chocolate cake milkshake that had cake chunks in it. He enjoyed it. I plan to give this place another chance for a better experience and try something different. It's definitely worth a try if you're in the area.

This place is so cute!!! The ice creams are super flavorful and it's very hard to stop at one. I wished I could try them all! Not to mention the great decor around the place. Definitely ready for some great foodie pictures. We went when the place was close to closing time. Whereas most staff but get frustrated with late customers, the staff here was ready to help!

This location is very small with only a handful of selections. There were 6 different macaroons to choose from. I got the coffee & pistachio, both had a great smell & taste. However, the texture was not the same. This place was not appetizing at all. Yountville, CA location definitely has everything to perfection & the selection is limitless.

It's really hit-or-miss at Milk Bar, but for the most part their desserts are way too sweet. I saw the chef's episode - Christina Tosi - on Chefs Table on Netflix and have been to Milk Bars across the country and I don't recommend anything really, which is a shame because I have lots of respect for the chef herself. Here's what I've had: It was our friends bday so they brought over these Milk Balls to Momofuku to end the meal. The only cute thing about it was the candle. It was just a crumbled up former-cake dusted with too much powdered sugar. I'd be embarrassed to serve this to people if I was the owner, even if it was free (it wasn't, we paid for this abomination) 1/10 Crack Pie - (now it's known as the milk bar pie) - again, too sweet, but edible. 5/10 Compost cookie kit - this is the only reason I'm bumping up my review. I brought home a tin with the ingredients from my trip to DC years ago and it was really fun to make and not bad at all! 8/10 Assorted cookies- got these for my bday this year and couldn't finish them. Way too sweet and hard/crumbly! 4/10 Overall everything is way too sweet at Milk Bar. I heard their cereal milk soft serve is good, so maybe... the 5th time I visit one of their locations... I can try it one day.

An apparent local institution and Tom Hanks recommended. The good: Classic frozen treat stand. Fresh, smooth custard (we saw a couple of the extruders working while waiting). Tons of flavor combinations with their snowstorms (mix in shakes or blizzards). Reasonable prices. The bad: While all three lines and drive through were open, the lines do take longer than I would think, even with what looked to be a full staff. While I appreciate that this is a tough job, with what propably seems like endless lines of hungry customers, I would have liked a bit more friendliness from our stereotypical surly teenager. The unknown: Perhaps I ordered wrong, but while delicious, my turtle sundae seemed a little light on the custard. I was left with quite a bit of hard chocolate/nutty shell and had to steal some spoons of custard from Cheddartarian's double custard root beer float. The other treats ordered by earlier guests looked quite a bit more generous. Ultimately, I would go back though, and that is as good a measure as anything.

My niece had been begging me to take her there as she had been raving about how great this place is. So, finally I took her and my daughter. Well, they loved it, but I have to say I wasn't impressed at all. The place is cute and the service was super friendly, but the cupcake I had was not too good. I just had their mini "black and white" and it was about 2 steps below a hostess cupcake. Very dry and very little taste. That's the story! I always tell the good, the bad and the ugly...

Very cute little spot just off of Roosevelt. I love the presentation of the ice cream in Chinese take out boxes, complete with fortune cookies. Love the flights, a sampling of five flavors plus fortune cookies presented in a muffin pan ($7.50). Love the dog friendly outdoor seating. And, most importantly, love the ice cream. My favorite ice cream flavor this visit? Peanut butter & jelly. Not the most juvenile flavor we ordered believe it or not. Those were Captain Crunch-berry and Lucky Charm based flavors ordered by the kids. Fear not. There are numerous choices for the adult palate as well.

Not really crazy about the ice cream. Some flavors are cloyingly sweet and hard to finish. Then there's the ingredients. This ice cream always tastes like it's got stabilizers and gums (and who knows what else) in it which I really don't like in my ice cream.

You have to get the cereal milk soft serve with extra cereal flakes (sweet and salty?!?! yaaassss!). You will turn over in your grave with regret if you don't try this dessert at least once! I guess my love for this soft serve comes from childhood nostalgia because I've only tasted something like this in Korea when I had cereal milk as a youngin! So freaking good! I also really enjoyed the crack pie and birthday cake!!!

Always wanted to try this place but the lines were always so long. We lucked out on this day as there wasn't a line so we walked in and ordered the 4 pc cake deal for 26 bucks We got a red velvet, a chocolate, a confetti birthday, and a rainbow cake with strawberry frosting. Cakes were good, I think the chocolate was made on site, the rest were in a sealed container so north sure They were all yummy

Not only does Mitchell's have the best ice cream around, this location is just the best. I love the open concept where you can see the factory setting behind the counter & two level seating for guests. There is a nice outdoor area to sit when the weather is nice that is a go-to in the summer time to hangout & enjoy your delicious ice cream. Favorite flavor: double chocolate chunk!!
This place is BOMB! My husband and I LOVE all their milkshakes. Definitely has turned into one of our go to sweets joint. Perfection!
Lots of flavors to choose from. I liked the chai tea and chocolate marshmallow I tried. Didn't care for the icing which was hard as a rock.
Fun place to try different flavor combos. We had chocoholic and frooty tooty and loved both. Waffle cones are fresh and yummy as well. Service is great!! Very clean.

Great quick stop for a cupcake or some ice cream, especially if it reminds you of home! Well, kind of, since I never made it to their Newport location, my only experience was ordering boxes for special occasions at the office, and those were good, looking pretty and pretty expensive! So it was great to see an actual store, it's probably similar for other people, they have great arrangements for every occasion. Here they have a "no-line" counter on the left side If you only buy cupcakes, or you can stay in line for the ice cream and cupcakes on the right side. We were strolling on the strip, so cupcakes to go was the best choice for us. All the cupcakes look good, and taste awesome, so it's a matter of preference, it's probably best to get more and share them.

I had an excellent experience at Churn. The dessert I had was phenomenal. I tried the lil Dragon freezie and it was delicious. I'm located on the west valley but I will definitely be making the long drive for Churn again. I highly recommend it. Fun staff and awesome environment, plus unique and tasty desserts!

Came here expecting some delicious ice cream and was not disappointed. I decided on mint choc chip with a sugar cone and it was exactly what I expected. The wait was longer than I expected, but I did see employees wearing gloves and the counters were clean. The store was well organized and easy to see prices. Sharda was my cashier and she was very friendly!

Have a dirty chai with almond milk, it's the best coffee I've ever had. Ever. Get a baguette with pimento and jam. And then get a chocolate torte and a salted caramel brownie. Perfect meal with an exemplary staff. I love this place!

I live in NODA and don't make it over here a lot, but when I do it's pretty good!! I do tend to get the same things but they work for me!! I typically order a cup of the soup *please note Im a huge soup lover!!! I can eat soup on the hottest day of the year i just LOVE it!! last two times I was in it was a potato leek with asparagus ( 95% sure) very good both times. I also have the Roast Beef with Borsin cheese on a baguette, my FAV!! I just want the option of having it to be bigger :) just a suggestion!! I'm not even going to try to start to name all of the pastries I've had from here, because it has been a lot!! All I can tell you is that almost all are great!! Some are not my favorite but you weed them out and find the ones you love!! In the future I'm going to try and make more of an effort to come here!! PS not sure if y'all heard but they are opening one in uptown across from The Green!!!
still great kouign amann. chocolate croissant was more cake like. macaron good at a better temp

The gluten free birthday cake truffles are ridiculous. Stopped by to pick some up, and was able to grab a few 3 packs. Service was fast and friendly. The cake bites are honestly perfect. They're soft and cake-y without being crumbly or having that "gluten-free" taste. No mealy, pasty texture. They're perfect, and it was too easy to get them.

Ugh! This was so disappointing! For someone to be the boss of all cakes, you'd think the cake would blow your mind, or at the absolute least, be some of the better cake you've ever tasted. Unfortunately that is not the case. My sister and I both got to-go items from here after a late night dinner at Buddy V's at the Venetian. We took them back to our hotel. I opted for the funfetti cake. It ended up being too late to eat mine and I don't like cold cake anyways (they refrigerate their cake which I get why they do it, but I prefer it be room temperature when I dine on it). I ended up eating it the next night and I took the first bite and must have made a face because my sister said "what's wrong?" and I said "Hmmm nothing... this just tastes like boxed cake. It's not really that good at all." I mean really, I can name NUMEROUS bakeries in Columbus, Oh (including our grocery store bakery, Giant Eagle) that are better than this place. I would say the cake part tasted like boxed funfetti cake and the frosting tasted cheaper than canned icing. So all in all, I think I'd actually prefer Pillsbury and would label it a tad better than this cake. I can't say for sure if the cake in their Hoboken location would be better, but I think it's safe to assume they'd use all the same ingredients because it's the same ownership. After this visit, I am wondering if the Cake Boss only became famous for his presentation of cakes, and not the actual taste. Anyways, main positive about this place is the line management. We were there so late on a Sunday that there wasn't much of a line, but there is someone waiting right there with an Ipad helping you out as soon as you walk in. Friendly, helpful staff. Anyways, I'd recommend passing on this. Take a walk down to The Linq and opt for a Sprinkles cupcake instead...

Visited The Vegan Doughnut Company today after much anticipation and hearing many rave reviews!! It 100% lived up to the hype! I tried the Fruity Cereal Milk and wow, it was delicious. The dough was so airy, fluffy, and light. It was sweet, but not overwhelmingly so. I also tried a few bites of their Easter-themed doughnuts, which were more of a cake doughnut consistency and also top-notch. The quality of these doughnuts is truly unmatched. I've heard a non-vegan say that these were the best doughnuts they've ever had. The location of the Vegan Doughnut Company is extremely convenient, on the main street of Lakewood. There is ample parking space in the lot for the shopping center behind the shop. Love to support this excellent local business.

You're forewarned to get to the bakery it is a mission from the Venetian guest parking lot. But the walk is worth it. We ordered a cake with Cristina for my mother in law and it came out fantastic! We got some goodies while there and all in all FRESH, DELICIOUS & perfectly sized for us! Major thank yous to Cristina she went above and beyond for us it is greatly appreciated! Thank you Cristina for making the cake even better than we thought! Definitely worth taking a trip into the Venetian for Carlos Bakery Team!

I came here every week overall I enjoyed the environment and service every time but I had a bad experience today. I feel like I'm not respected by the barista/cashier - Jesse (that's what she told me not sure if she made it up). I'd like some milk for my dripped coffee but she did not seem like to help me with it. She was reluctant to get me the milk but instead trying to have me used the cream on the table. That is not something I need and when I insist on getting the milk, she took the milk out from the fridge with a lot of aversion on her face. I feel like being discriminated as she treats other caucasian customers with a MUCH MORE friendly manner. I feel like your store needs an ethical training especially for Jesse.

Like In N Out, they have seriously long lines. Their icecream is slooooooooo good. Love their chocolate chip cookies. It just melts in your mouth. Their Sprinkles Cupcake ATM machine is ingenious. We need these machines everywhere.

I tried the wild berry lavender in a cup. It was delicious and they gave me a waffle cone piece on the side which was a great touch! They also provide self-serve water which I greatly appreciate. Only problem was that when I was there I had to go to the bathroom really badly but they don't have one :/
Very slow customer service. The lady wasn't the most pleasant person. With the line , you can tell such a high demand however very slow in getting crepe. You ll need 45-50 min to get your crepe

I came here pretty excited, you know reading the reviews and all. The parking lot is really small in front but there are more in the back. The ice cream shop is shared by a restaurant which is called the Windsor. The decoration is really beautiful and feels just like those old candy shops where they have sweets everywhere! Anyways I started sampling ice creams and they were just okay. Surprisingly I really didn't like any of them. They were creamy, sweet but the flavor just really wasn't there. There was no uniqueness about any of the flavors. I did get candy corn ice cream and even though it was good, it got boring after the first few bites. I understand everyone's fascination with this place so I am definitely in the minority but I really didn't like this ice cream shop as much as I thought I would

This is my favorite ice cream place in Cleveland's west side. My most recent visit was specifically to try the ube ice cream. I also got taro so I could taste the difference between the two. I prefer ube, which was more flavorful and sweeter to me. Also, it is a pretty shade of purple! There are many other unique flavors here, and it changes weekly. Vegan flavors are available too. The best way to keep up with the ever changing menu is to follow their Instagram. I'm hoping they bring back the green tea soft serve soon. The shop is small, with outdoor seating and no indoor seating. Parking only has about five spaces, so it is easier to park on the street. The shop itself is super cute and has artwork of dogs eating ice cream on the wall and on the cups. It's just a perfect spot to hang out at during the summer.

Always loved going to their San Diego location when I lived there. Perfect place to grab pastries for any gathering. All their pastries are made fresh (fresh bread!!!) and kept in display boxes for you to grab with tongs. My favorite things to grab there are the ube breads, chocolate, and their hot dog rolls. Sorry I'm not sure of the exact names but it's pretty self explanatory. They do have a selection of drinks as well to help wash down all their delicacies. Unfortunately the location they are at in China town smells of fresh sewage which severely takes away from the sweet aromas that should engulf you when you walk home. Other then that, some of the workers are a bit rude, even the supervisor (it says so on her badge) gave me attitude because I couldn't hear her through her mask. #covidperks other then that, I'll still come here when I'm in the area to treat myself to a few pastries and try not to over do it.

Went for the toffee banofi but ended up making my own mix......Triple play coconut sorbet, peaberry espresso sorbet, coconut cashew curry ice cream with homemade brittle and caramel sauce. WOW WEEEEEEEE WOW!!!!! is all I can say. For once I can say there is something that rivals gelato. I will definitely be back!
The graham central station is hands down my favorite flavor!! Probably one of my favorite ice cream spots in Vegas!
Raised prices to 24.95 per dozen from 18.95. A 32% increase! Good donuts but not worth that price. Way to stick it to your customers.

ECCENTRIC FRENCH There is a reason the line is out the door. This place is the place to be for great desserts, savory fillings and great beverages. The eccentric decor adds to the ambience and gives you things to look at while you are in line. The line is long, but goes quickly. Keep going in the back they have more seating than you think. My daughter enjoyed her eclair while I had the pot of chocolate. She had the turkey and bacon. I had roast beef and monchego. We brought home pastries for breakfast. Great value. Wonderful quality.

Okay so I'm not one to normally post reviews but OH MAN THIS PLACE!!!!! I've had their ice cream twice. The first time my roommate brought me home just a cup of strawberry ice cream. It was probably the best strawberry ice cream I've had! The second time, I went to the ice cream shop. It is in a cute little hidden village of shops. When we first walked in we were greeted immediately by the nice owners! They let us try all the flavors we wanted. I tried the Fat Elvis (peanut butter ice cream w/ caramelized bananas and bacon). It was delicious. I also had to try the honey lavender because I have heard great things and it was so light and yummy. But I was there for one thing. The donut melt!!!! Donuts + ice cream?! What could be better?? I got the Cookie Monster (blue cookies and cream flavor with chocolate chip cookies, Oreos and vanilla wafers). They warm up the donut sandwiches and they are so perfect. And you get one free topping! My boyfriend got the Leslie Knope which is a European waffle ice cream sandwich. He chose the Fat Elvis flavor. It was also delicious! I would much rather support a local small shop and this is just the place I will be picking. If you haven't already, GO TRY IT!!! You won't be disappointed!
The best donuts you will ever eat. A little piece of heaven! I recommend Jack Frost to everyone!!!

Got a Rick and Morty cake made for my daughter with Devils food chocolate cake and oreo cream filling with fondant. I am not a fondant lover but this was amazing! It was delicious and my daughter loved it. The staff are all very friendly. Money well spent. They also worked with me and answered any questions or concerns I had. I'll be ordering more future cakes.

While I was in Paris, my boyfriend was in Las Vegas...oddly enough in the fake Paris hotel...you can guess who won the battle of emailing Eiffel Tower pictures. I decided he too needed to smuggle baked goods in his luggage. I think he did a better job than me. I only asked for bouchons, but I was also given a chocolate tart. I think my heart stopped for a couple seconds while eating it, and I'm not sure if it's because I shouldn't have eaten the whole thing by myself or because it tasted of chocolate heaven. Even though it had been in the freezer for a couple days, it was still pretty damn amazing. The bouchons were just not that amazing in retrospect after the tart. They were good, but I can make a glorified brownie too if necessary. I am far too lazy for a tart. I would eat everything again though, and then some more, don't get me wrong.

SEE ATTACHED PHOTOS!! Cleveland HOMEMADE Ice-Cream. I LOVE Honey Hut Ice-Cream. I visited the State Road location with my friend Lesly N. in early September 2019. I ordered the Honey Chai and Sea Salt Caramel on a waffle cone ($3.50). My friend bought the Honey Chai and the Chocolate Pecan flavour on a cup with sprinkles on top. We sat outside on a nice weather day. There is no seating inside because it is set up as a walk-up ordering place. Outside has benches to sit on including an area with a white canopy like covering that has benches below. ICE-CREAMS -- There are a bunch of flavours to choose from. The honey chai is the perfect combination of honey and chai. This is a very unique flavour. The sea salt caramel is sweet and delightful if you enjoy caramel. I can't wait to return. Ice cream at Honey Hut makes life a little bit sweeter :) **** - 149 total reviews in 2019 - 358 total overall Yelp reviews - Reviewed on 7 December 2019

I had never heard of Milk Bar until it was suggested to me on social media. I'm apparently easily influenced when it comes to food ads, because I started thinking about their cake often! I considered ordering it to be shipped from New York, but I'm actually glad I didn't spend the money because what I tried at the Vegas location wasn't the greatest. I got a slice of birthday cake, which was straight out of the fridge. Do people like cold cake? I really dislike it. I debated letting it sit out for a while, but decided to just go for it. It tasted like week old refrigerated cake, heavy and overly moist. I did appreciate the icing though, it melted in my mouth! I wasn't able to eat more than 1/4 of the cake slice, but I did eat a bunch of icing because it was pretty good. I'd love to try a fresh slice of their birthday cake! For $14, I just expected so much more. I left feeling pretty disappointed.

Ice Cream Social is incredible! I started buying pints from Katrina during the pandemic - I've probably bought at least 20 so far. The flavors are unique and delicious. And the ice cream stays reasonably soft in the freezer, which is a huge bonus. My favorite thing to get at the shop is a flight so that I can try 3 different flavors, because it is hard to choose just one! I highly recommend getting waffle cone pieces as your topping. It's too hard to choose a favorite flavor! I don't like the ones with jam as much (personal preference), but I've enjoyed every flavor I have tried.

Wishing this was a fivestar-er, but man we're bummed. It was hard to find this place at night, no illuminated signage. Once we found it, we were pumped and the girl who welcomed us in was nice. Unfortunately, although we were the only people there... And the only people in the parking lot.. Repeating myself here this joint was not busy, pretty much everything we came for was sold out. The marshmallow you see in every picture on Yelp? Sold Out. What bothers me about that? How do you run out of your signature item, especially when it's (I'm assuming here) not homemade. Go to the grocery store, buy mallows. Problem solved. Same with the red velvet macaroons. I happened to order the last one, leaving my boyfriend to pick from the remaining flavors (Carmel was also sold out). Ice cream flavors were good and the macaroon was tasty, but for $11+ dollars?! No. Especially with the inconvenience of ordering from a limited menu and the atmosphere being kinda meh. Just... No.

This hole in the wall ice cream shop is fresh and gorgeous. The store is lined with gorgeous art prints for sale. Try Purple Rain, formerly known as Blueberry Muffin. It is far away from me, but definitely worth the drive.

85C is a mandatory stop at Shanghai Plaza. My family, friends and colleagues love the pastries. We would have a box of 85°C at my work's break room and conference room at least twice a month lol. Selection: Assorted pastries are freshly baked and more affordable than other bakeries. It seems like there are always new goodies every time we visit. The beverage menu was just decent, we enjoyed the iced coffee and sea salt jasmine iced tea. We really just come here for the pastries lol Service: Staff is friendly, also hardworking! They would come in and out to restock the pastries as some of the goodies get sold within minutes of after the previous restock lol! Parking: FREE. Shanghai Plaza parking lot just outside the bakery. We prefer parking in the back at W Pioneer Ave. & Arville St. then just stroll around the plaza since it gets really packed in the front. Highly recommend!

Small shop with a lot of variety. They have a lot you can park in and a couple of tables with benches outside. Inside is just the baked goods, no area for seating. Baked goods: ranged from cake slices, macarons, to pastries. We shared: - lobster tail: crunchier than I expected but I enjoyed it a lot. The cream filling is light, airy, and not overly sweet. Together, my husband described it like eating cereal. With the almost milky creaminess from the whipped cream and the crunchy pastry shell - New York crumb cake: was worried the crumbs would be the only good part but the cake is very moist and good! Overall a solid cake - horn (strawberries and cream): my least favorite, the pastry tasted undercooked. It was almost good. The filling seemed like it was just packaged strawberry cream cheese.

We came here for a sweet bite after eating across the street at Federal Pizza. The line was out the door, but no one seemed to mind waiting. I was too busy looking at all the retro candy from my childhood, so when I got to the front of the line...I had no clue what I wanted and didn't want to hold the line up. So, one of the gals suggested the Peanut Butter ice cream (score!) and the pretzel cone I had already planned to try...because...it's a pretzel and a cone! I loved the creamy natural tasting peanut butter ice cream, but the cone was a bit of a let down. It was a tad too salty and not light and airy like a regular pretzel. It was thick and on the crunchy side. So, I think I'll skip it the next time I go in. We enjoyed sitting out back though! Make sure you make your way back there instead of sitting out front where the line is a bit in the way.

This is the only reason to go to Las Vegas. Who cares about the bright lights, the big buildings, when you can eat delicious ice cream!?!? I went here on a Friday night around 7:30 PM. There were four people working and the line was into the street. However, the line move fairly quickly and even if it was longer I would've waited. I decided on a fourth Cooper sampler which is by and large the best option on the menu. I had blueberry cobbler, chocolate marshmallow, banana cream pie and Keylime pie. The person who took my order was knowledgeable about all of the ice cream's and knew what was in each of them. I like the banana cream pie ice cream the best followed by the Keylime pie followed by the blueberry cobbler and chocolate marshmallow tied. I also thought that the four items sampler was super affordable based on how delicious it was and how much ice cream there with us. There is no reason to ever go to Las Vegas and not stop here for ice cream even if it is a little bit out-of-the-way. The only other tip is to my knowledge there are no bathrooms and there isn't much seating outside so that could be a challenge.

I was not impressed with the Donut Bar. The French toast donut and latte I got were pretty good, but everything else I tried was flavourless. Like a lot of other reviews mentioned, the sugar topping on the creme brÃ»lÃ©e donut was way too thick, the red velvet donut was very dry and didn't taste like anything, and the Nutella donut was less dry but still had almost no flavour.

All I can say is delicious!!! These donuts are.very indulgent, can't visit to often lol but amazing. My favorite ones were the Nutella donut and the birthday surprise with an oreo . Their portions r huge so u don't need to purchase many to share. Must come back!

The interior styling and decor of this cafe is incredible with usage of antiques and vintage items to create a cozy, artsy aesthetic. The Butterwood offers a variety of succulent gourmet pastries and cakes with surprising flavors to delight every taste bud. In addition, many coffees and teas are available to accompany your sweet treat. Service is always excellent and the baristas are extremely helpful answering any and all questions. If you want to stop somewhere for a great (and unique) baked good and hot beverage in an interesting setting, you must stop here!
This place is just the bomb!!! Love all different flavors and Tuesday specials!!! Everyone is friendly
Home grown Ice !! Have to swing here... Trending and always new trys! Swing by this place after a slice of pizza across the street from Grads Pizza

On a Friday night in October, the door says cash only which is odd since there is a coin shortage. I entered the door and no greeting from the cashier. No one was inside at all. I love looking at the Ghirardelli chocolates packaged for Xmas. I just a small chocolate bar since I borrowed few bucks from my sister. The chocolate bar was delicious and hit the spot. 2 stars no greeting when entering 4 stars plenty of chocolate to choose

Cute place in the cut. I was looking for somewhere to get pastries after dinner and Amelie's had a very little selection that night so I found this on Yelp and I'm glad I did. They only allow 2 in at a time so be prepared to stand outside if it is a busy time. They move you in and out pretty quickly though. I got a cannoli and crumb cake. Both were delicious and hit the spot. There was a nice selection of goodies so I'm sure anyone can find something they like. Now I know where I can get something sweet.
Wow. Small shop with small selection of ice cream BUT really good. Lady working there extremely helpful. Fair prices for quality hand made ice cream. Hard to find but again well worth it.

I've received a few recommendations from friends about this spot! It's close to my home but slightly off the main Central shopping area. You'll see it on the other side of hwy 74. The shop itself is small, cute, and smells incredible! Park in the open gravel lot and enjoy your pastries on the picnic tables, no inside seating. The employees were helpful when I shared it was my first time and wanted to try the "favorites". They recommended the tiramisu, lemon bar, s'mores bar, or slice of cheesecake. There was cookies, puff pastries filled with cream, brownies, macarons, and more! I wanted everything. The lemon bar was great, the s'mores bar was del delicious, and the lobster tail was awesome! I can't wait to come back and try more.

Tried this place after hearing about the hype. Had to wake up extra early so try all the flavors before they sold out. This was not worth the hype, we got a dozen doughnuts since we don't live in Vegas. The special doughnuts weren't anything special. The creme brulee didn't have enough filling nor did the other flavors. All the doughnuts tasted normal, flavors weren't special or "wow" about them compared to most normal doughnut shops. I've had better doughnuts in the east coast. This was such a disappointment.
Great Ice Cream every time I have been there the ice cream is awesome the customer service is great 5 stars all the way

I finally had my first Mitchell's Ice Cream experience. Many of my Cleveland friends have bragged about their ice cream, so I had some high expectations...and they were definitely met! My first time there I ordered the Caramel Sea Salt (caramelized brown sugar and sea salt). It was delicious. The prices are a bit steep for a scoop of ice cream ($3.35) but when you get to the front of the line and see how big the scoop is and how tasty it is, it's not such a bad price after all. My second time there I ordered chocolate peanut butter cup, again a heaping scoopful. The chocolate ice cream itself wasn't anything special from any other high end ice cream, but there were so many big chunks of peanut butter cup, enough for every bite. My boyfriend ordered the chocolate malt ($4.95) both times (btw he tends to consider himself a malt aficionado). The first time they gave him a chocolate shake by mistake. It was good, but it was made with chocolate ice cream (I guess chocolate malts are not made with chocolate ice cream) and wasn't the malt he'd ordered...so he was disappointed. The second time we finally got the malt (this time made with vanilla ice cream and chocolate syrup). He said he liked it, although not the best. To me the malt flavoring wasn't very noticeable and I think Sweet Moses makes better malts. Mitchell's put more malt flavoring in your malts! They use Hartzler's milk, I have never had their milk, but their egg nog is to die for (save that for another review) so I can only assume their milk is something special. Also it seems that most of the premium ice cream shops in Cleveland tend to use their milk. The store and building itself is also pretty impressive. You can go upstairs and view the entire kitchen from above, watching them make ice cream is cool. Also you know there's no funny stuff going on in there if you can see everything. Be warned, the lines can be long and seem impossible to get to the front in any reasonable time, but rest assured, there are a lot of people working the counter and those lines move really fast. Oh and they also let me bring my dog in with me to order my ice cream. I love places that are dog friendly! So many more flavors of ice cream still to try...a few blocks from home...I will be down there a lot this summer. Let's just hope my waistline can take all these visits.

I was there at the grand opening at 9. got there around 8:00am and was one of the first 25 people . They had UNLV cheerleaders to cheer and had a great opening. The bread was nice and fresh. Respect for the managers to have crowd control and not let it look like a Hong Kong protest inside with people grabbing bread off the trays before they hit the shelf. They handled that pretty well. I got everything I could on my tray. two mugs and the yardstick for the first 100 customers. The above review is 5 stars worthy for the morning. the reason why I put a one star is for people who are curious and for the managers to look at how they did cause they care about the business and need customer feedback. I went back there at night because I gave most of the bread pastries away to my coworkers since we had a birthday celebration. I did not have a chance to try the matcha custard bread, milk pudding bun, the croquette bun. etc. I went back hoping there was still more at night. instead it was mostly subpar items like muffins and the egg tarts. None of the premium items I saw in the morning or mentioned above or the ones you see in the morning review posts. It was just pumping out the same bread and put it in three different places. I saw the berry tart like in three different shelves and muffins that anyone can go get at Starbucks. It was just selling bread at that point for profit since there was a demand there, but also because they probably ran out of ingredients for the other items. Here is the reason where they screwed up. Since the morning. it was pretty chaotic with all the excitement. I forgot to ask if the free yardstick was refillable or not. I heard the regional divisional manager say this is the first of its kind for Las Vegas since it has Vegas themes on the free items. I could not hear if he said "free" refills or " no refills for the yardstick. I went back at night to ask and clarify. I asked three employees and they did not know. Till I asked the lady at the drink section kindly if it was free refill or not. The cashier next to her heard me and said in an angry tone. NO REFILL. then mumbled to her coworker " they brought it up in the meeting." the one I asked kindly went to her manager and asked and she came back and told me no without yelling No REFILL like the other cashier did. I accepted it since i wasnt sure due to all the noise in the morning. The one star is for the rude cashier at the front. All it takes is one thing to ruin the whole experience. the customers are the driving force for the business, but if they have cashiers not able to handle the customers, then people reading should be aware to expect it. Bread was perfect, grand opening was perfect. Ask a question and get an angry response from another employee and I am willing to spend the time to write this one star review. Do yourself a favor. Dont go there at night and grab the leftover inventory. Wait till the hype goes down and they train their employees to be nice and courteous to the customers.

Great spot to get some really good ice cream. We like to get the sweet sundae where you can choose 4 different kinds of ice cream, comes with a cookie, brownie and a toasted marshmallow. This is a great item to share. I have also got the sorbet, strawberry and coconut which is very refreshing as well. Typically on the weekends they have enough employees to handle the line. When I recently went this past weekend, they do not have any seating inside only about two tables outside. Love to come here when we are in the area!

Been here a few times and the desserts are definitely good. There's always a crowd and they can run out of some of their more popular desserts. There's a good variety, unique decor, and the line moves pretty fast. If you come during peak hours it can definitely be hard to find a seat and you may have to stand in a line that goes out the door and wraps around the corner. The prices I think are high for Charlotte, they're pretty much what I would pay in LA for the same thing but the desserts are good. And it's one of the few places in Charlotte that's not a bar but open late.

AMAZING! AWESOME! A whole new level in donuts... Very friendly, customer oriented staff, easy street parking but I live close and walk... Get in early because the line begins at 7am. Definitely a pilgrimage for donut connoisseurs!

Absolutely delicious gluten free cupcakes and cookies. The GF red velvet cupcake is moist and the GF chocolate chip cookie is soft and delectable! Can't even tell they are gluten free! I also love their frosting shots, since I am an icing lover. Always a dependable place to grab a gluten free treat -- The only con is that you may wait in line for an obscene amount of time.

I was hangin out at third space and noticed this new joint in the compound. Super friendly staff that encouraged me to try their ice cream filled donut with cereal crammed in. I've gotta say this thing is un-f'n-believable! Have you ever ate an ice cream sandwich with a cookie where after the first bite the ice cream shoots out the back side and all over your pants? Whelp, Novel has solved the riddle and they adddded cereal! Wow. Just wow. I'd give this place 6 stars if I could. I'm def going back.
Amazing chocolate and ice cream, in a fun little corner off the strip. Nice gift shop also.

We closed an evening out with a stop at this open all night bakery. I couldn't believe how many people were waiting in line, but this had to be a good sign, right? The line moved very quickly just as the decisions on what to try had to be made fast. There were 4 of us and together we purchased two vanilla eclairs, two coconut macaroons, chocolate cream puff and raspberry chocolate tart along with fresh brewed coffee. I thought the prices were very reasonable considering the quality. I was told the salted caramel brownies are very popular. The French bohemian decor with mismatched tables, chairs, and odd assortment of pictures on the walls adds to the vibe. Definitely worth stopping in to give yourself a treat.

Attention ice cream and donut lovers! Out in Phx. off of Grand Ave & 11th. ave. behind the Third Space green building. You gotta try this very tasty homemade ice cream and floats at Novel Ice cream! Fun and eclectic flavors to choose from! From Honey & Lavender, pistachio, cookie monster (blue), tangerine sherbet, and many other delicious mouthwatering flavors. Including chocolate, and strawberry. Even their award winning Madagascar vanilla! You can choose to have any flavor ice cream filled in a donut with or without cereal toppings. Or a waffle filled ice cream sandwich! An ice cream float with your choice of soda. Or just the simple ice cream scoop in a cup or a cone. Friendly employees and the prices are not so high. Plenty of space to sit out front and enjoy your tasty treat and the warm sunshine. Now off I go and burn off this ice cream.

Presti's is one of my favorite places in Cleveland! I went here all the time when I lived in little Italy. They have a huge variety of pastries ranging from m&ms cookies to fancy miniature cheesecakes. They also serve a variety of lunch type foods, like sandwiches, stromboli and pizza by the slice. OH, and of course there's the gelato! So yummy! There really is something for everyone here. Word of warning though, they are usually quite busy! Make sure to take a number before looking at all those pastries. :)

This place is awesome! The atmosphere. The music. The people. Yes, yes, yes! The Maiko Special is so good. Normally these layered desserts are super (too) sweet but this one is amazing. You can taste the flavors of each item in the cup and nothing is too sweet. The mochi is on point.

While we stop by Bouchon every time we're in Vegas, I had somehow never made it to the bakery..... what a mistake! I was suppose to have half a bite of the baked strawberry croissant and accidentally ate half of it while on 7th heaven...SO perfectly flaky and delicious. My friend also bought some macarons and MAN they were delicious...

STOP!!! This is what I observed during my visit tonight Saturday March 20, 2021 at 9:15 PM. The same staff member that takes your order and money goes to the dipping case to scoop your ice cream without washing his hands or wearing a pair of gloves. At best, this is not sanitary and worst they could be spreading COVID-19. We all know that money is filthy and we should wash our hands after handling it. The unsafe practices at the establishment should be criminal. God know just how many unsuspecting customers caught the COVID-19 virus from this place.

Oh my goodness! What a gem. I had the dough melt with sweet cream and honey. Whoever thought of using a donut for an ice cream sandwich is a genius. Best dessert I've had in Phoenix. Love the small and fresh batches of ice cream, which when paired with a warm donut is heavenly. Great service from the owner's too. I will be back again.

I really wanna really like this place but everytime I go there is always loaded of people there. The price for macaroons are making it hard for me to like them. I know it doesn't cost much to make it and the stuff can be NICER BUT THEY AREN'T so it's hard to like this place. They see us as $$$ or annoying customer that ask for loaded stuff. They only reason this place is the hot spot right now is because theirs no other's 24/7 bakery near by or in Charlotte period. $2:30 for one.macroons is just too high.
Pistachio macarons are the best. Also bought a large heart-shaped sugar cookie for my bf. So freaking adorable. He only had 2 bites of it though. :X On the pricier end, but totally worth every penny.

Growing up Presti's was the spot for donuts. It's so much more now. Prepared pastas, pizza slices, gelato, pastries. I'm not sure what they do best now. That's probably the only problem I have with them. That being said they do a lot of things very well.

The ladies who were there were so sweet, serving us at 7:59pm when they closed at 8. I really appreciated that! Also the prices were extremely reasonable. That being said... the chocolate on the bonbons were all cracked and bubbly, clearly not tempered right. I ordered an espresso bonbon which I did enjoy. It oozed a sweet espresso goo in the middle, though the sugar granuals were present, having not been melted when mixed. The rum-dipped dark chocolate bonbon was the real displeasure. It was clearly milk chocolate, and dry at that. And the inside was so disappointing I had to write something. The "rum filing" was a congealed sugar solid that tasted nothing of rum. I've never not wanted to finish a chocolate treat. Maybe they had been in the case for too long as the bonbons definitely varies depending on ingredients. Their cupcakes are out of this world, though.
Wow, just had a cinnamon cupcake and it's probably the best I've ever had! Tasted just like a snickerdoodle cookie. Don't miss this spit on the LINQ Promenade. It's full of little hidden gems.
No military discount here. Minimal seating at this ice cream store. 2 stars, because the employees were unfriendly.

I do not understand the negative reviews for this place! After watching the Netflix documentary I couldn't wait to try it during our stay in Vegas. We got the B-Day truffles, B-Day Latte, Cereal Milk Latte, Crack Pie, Bagel Bomb and Birthday Cake (don't judge, we were four people hungry for breakfast). The employees were so so nice and let us try all their soft serves (delicious). All our food was INCREDIBLE, I would definitely be back!!

Good assortment of pastries, as well as a solid sandwich lineup makes this place a good spot for breakfast OR lunch. The large , cozy interior creates a laid back experience as well. The fact that it's open 24/7 , which for a business in Charlotte is a rarity ensures a good late-night java joint also.

I have been wanting to try this place forever, but I've avoiding it because like ever other local I hate the strip. I was in the Venetian, and accidentally ran into this little gem. I was unprepared, shocked, excited! I knew that I wanted to try the macaroons. At the $3.50 a pop, I could only justify getting one. I settled on my favorite flavor, pistachio, and ordered a chocolate chip cookie as well. The macaroon was overly sweet. To me it tasted like an Andes mint flavored macaroon, so maybe they use mint for color? There was only a subtle hint of pistachio. I was completely disappointed. The macaroons in the freezer section at Walmart are 10 times better. The chocolate chip cookie was okay. The chocolate chips were fantastic, but the cookie was just average. Definitely not something I'd go back for. If you're on the Strip, there are far better options that are more deserving of your money and caloric intake. Skip this one!

The French Toast ice cream was EXTREMELY salty to the point where a few bites in could give you hypertension. We also tried the Birthday Cake Milkshake that was also bad. It seemed like the milk or cream had gone bad. On top of that it's odd that an ice cream place in a casino wouldn't offer tap or iced water.

Rule: if there is no line, go and grab ice cream! This was the original Jeni's location in Charlotte and still super popular. The staff are super friendly, masked-up and ready to go. The stand alone building only has counter seating and the line moves through pretty fast. Lots of outdoor tables to sit at or the large concrete steps behind the store. I really only went in here to get a few pints to take home, so I'm not sure how they are handling samples during Covid, but they always gave you separate sampling spoons and the the staff always wore gloves before the pandemic. Southend is pretty lucky to have a cool spot like Jeni's to enjoy after going to one of the many restaurants nearby.

It's not a sketchy dog groomer anymore with bars on the window. Get the cake!! It is an enormous piece for $6, moist, killer icing, not too sweet but such a treat yourself treat. I hope to try the extensive macaroons selection next and get a corner piece brownie - equal parts crispy and gooey. The one pass for me was the cookie bar, the cookies included weren't my favorite.

Oh. My. Gosh. This was the most delicious thing I've ever tasted. I got the doughmelt with the chocolate cherry pistachio ice cream and it was heaven. The three other people I was with tried different ice cream flavors with their melts and everyone was in love! We will definitely be back. The only downside is that they're not located closer to me!

Went to this location on a Saturday and night and man it was packed at midnight like it was peak hours. It was smaller than the other locations I have been to and a lot of items were sold out as well. I wanted fruit tart but they didn't have any. The long was line too considering it was midnight but i guess that may be the norm for this location.

My first time trying macaroons was at Bouchon! I work nearby & always hear everyone raving about how delicious they are so of course I had to try them for myself! I didn't know which kind to try so I got the variety box with six different flavors. I'm not entirely sure what those flavors were but they were delicious!

I was out of hope looking for a nice bakery in Charlotte to get my pastry fix when I stumbled on this one in the Noda district. Walking through the door you're greeted with an eclectic decor that I the only way I might be able to describe would be chic french hipster. They have an interesting and varied selection of pastries and chocolates that were fun to look at and delicious as well! I went for lunch with a friend and she had the ginger rice soup, and I had the asparagus leek soup. I'm not a fan of ginger so her soup was ok, but the asparagus leek soup was excellent! Creamy and smooth it was a dream. We also split a croque monsieur and it was done perfectly. Greasy, a little crisp on the outside, with the mustard giving a nice kick to the sandwich. Now for the dessert portion we had a strawberry and chocolate croissant, salted caramel brownie, and creme brulee with a small french press. I feel like the strawberry and chocolate croissants could have used a little more filling but they were quite good. The salted caramel brownie I really needed more salt to cut through the creamy sugar of the caramel, but then again I tend to like my snacks a bit less sweet. The creme brulee was the winner of the dessert round. Nice and crisply caramelized top with a not too sweet center. Amelie's was a great find in the Noda area and offers free wifi, a nice place to relax, and a varied crowd with pastry choices for everyone. It's now on my list of places to visit frequently!

Love this bakery , a Las Vegas gem. Have to be careful because don't want to gain a 100 pounds, all their stuff is do good. Specially love the chocolate croissants. Our little grandbaby loved it too. No visit to Las Vegas is complete without visiting this bakery. Ps. Should have checked in when we were there.
AMAZEBALLZZZZZ!!!! Great customer service, fun staff and they know their products! I can't wait to go back very soon! And let's not forget they got great music!

I was so excited to go to Milk from all of the pictures i see on social media. I got 3 things at Milk. First since I am a cake lover I got a slice of Birthday Cake which is a vanilla rainbow cake, rainbow cake crumbs, sprinkles, vanilla frosting. The cake was moist and and the frosting did have a big vanilla taste but as far as cakes go it was a little underwhelming. Really nothing special with that slice of cake. The second thing I ordered was the Crunchy Cereal Shake which was made with milk, cornflakes, brown sugar and a pinch of salt. It did taste like cereal like I expected but all I really did was pay $9 to drink cereal, nothing special there either. The last thing I ordered which was the best thing was the Crack Pie. I can see why this is there fan favorite because it is addicting as if you were doing crack. Haha. The Crack Pie has a toasted oat crust and a gooey butter filling. So you get that crunch of the crust with that creamy gooey filling. This is the one thing you must have at Milk, but overall this place was pricey and not as exciting as it has been made out to be. BrandonFitFoodie

Ok, how adorable is this place? Parking is limited up front but there is a parking lot on the side with plenty of room. Walking in is like hopping back in time. It is a really cute little ice cream parlor. They have a bunch of fun nostalgic candy for sale too. My mom and I shared one of their seasonal freezes and it was so good. I am really glad we split it, they were nice enough to put it into two cups for us too. It was really good but also really sweet and I definitely would not have been able to finish one myself.

I love the different varieties of chocolate covered pretzels they have. The chocolate to pretzel ratio is what it like lol (if that makes sense). It's not too much chocolate coated on the pretzel. They have this Turtle Pretzel that is sooo freakin' yummy. They only thing I craved today was pretzels lol and I ran there to pick up a few...it was hard to leave the place because everything look so dee-lish. The popcorn they have can be a little daring. I tried I think some kind of Jalapeno popcorn and even though I love hot and spicy stuff...that left me in tears lol really! But the carmel corn, when it's warm, is really good!

I have seen Milk Bar all over my Instagram feed. They're cups are trendy, the presentation is perfect for your feed (and for feeding). I was delighted when I visited Las Vegas and saw they had a location in the Cosmopolitan. The wannabe Instagram influencer came out in me and was ecstatic to try this cereal + milk ice cream combo. I've never been one to drink the milk at the bottom of my cereal bowl so I was didn't think I was going to enjoy this treat as much as I did. The corn cereal flavor really shined. It was creamy, sweet, and crunchy. A perfect treat for a warm Las Vegas afternoon. I would love to visit Milk Bar's other locations and try more of their creations.

I'm just here for the Brown Butter Almond Brittle, the best thing since sliced bread. After attending a Yelp event where my only regret was not choosing three servings of this ice cream. Needless to say that I found myself here again not long after. Don't be intimidated by the line outside of the door at Jeni's. It's only that way because there isn't much room inside for a line. They should consider getting those line makers that they have at the movie theatre so people aren't outside in the blistering heat. The lines move quick and the staff is very kind and diligent about moving customers down the counter, as there are three identical ice cream stations. I later went on a mission to find the ice cream in stores. Pints were $8 at Publix.

Wow. I can't believe how complacent people are. I loved everything that I bought. Don't believe the reviews until you go and try it for yourself. These "one star" and "two star" people are just unhappy and miserable people.
Over 300 reviews and still 5 out of 5 had me curious and this place did not disappoint! Super good! Love it!

I really didn't enjoy the doughnut sandwich I got. It looked amazing but the taste didn't match. The service was great, I felt welcomed and taken care of... I took one bite and throw it in the trash. It was pretty much a waste of money for me- I wish that someone nearby wanted my partially eaten food so it didn't go in the trash...

I love their dessert. I came here every time I go to Cosmo. I have gotten their Milk Bar pie (crack pie) and their cereal milk soft serve. The first time I got their cereal milk soft serve we didn't know it comes with the actual cereal on it. Just got one with my boyfriend and friend, we all got cereal milk soft serve and this time they all came with cereal topping. DELICIOUS! Their crack pie was good too. I usually get a slice and share. For some people it can be little bit too rich, but if you handle sweet like me. I think it's actually good. Crack pie reminded me of ginger snap chewy cookie. There are so many other goodies that I want to try. Will definitely try other things next time. Stay tunes.
I am gluten free so my options were limited, but I was happy there were options at all! The gluten free birthday cake truffles were AMAZING!!!

Small bakery in the middle of the Venetian, behind the escalators going down around the Phantom Theater. After going to the Napa location numerous times, this one is sad to stop by and give 2 stars to =(. But they only had 4 types of macarons, service was kind of weird/awkward, and the cappuccino was not worth $4 (it was watered down/really weak). Chocolate almond croissant was dry. I'd only come back because the macarons taste the same, hopefully the Napa location opens back up soon!

Honestly I had their cakes and crack pie. Have not been to the actual store but was given their Birthday Cake and Crack Pie. Birthday Cake could be a little bit "too sweet" for some but to me it was more rich than sweet. The Crack PIe is the business. If you freeze it it's even better. Again very rich and flavorful and a cross between pecan pie and peanut brittle (without the nuts) but it's one of those things where the whole pie is in front of you and 10 mins later you look down and nothing is there cause your fat ass ate the whole damn thing without realizing it. It's that good imo. Will def go to the store to try other items like the Cookies and Cereal Milk.
LOVE this delightful little place except on Friday & Saturday nights!! - SO busy but still worth it. ;)

I can't eat gluten but the coffee here is amazing. The customer service is impeccable and they remember you each time you go. I always bring in people from out of town and local groups. They are fantastic two children and go above and beyond to help you find the donut that you want. If it's available the French toast donut is a must-try. If you get there at the end of the day they will give you a deal on Donuts which is great because you never get yesterday's Donuts.

First off let me say...this is a place we frequent due to the fact they are open 24/7 and have FRENCH PRESS coffee!!! It is like being able to truly just "get away" from the norm around Charlotte. I also think they have the best french baguette I have ever had. Before taking a road trip's to NC vineyards...we swing by and grab a baguette and chicken salad croissant...and a sweet something too! Amelie's to none compares in Charlotte!!! The ONLY thing they could add is some great music mix in the seating areas...sometimes it is almost too quiet depending upon what time you are there :+) The staff is really great too!!

Overrated. Good ice cream and I like to support local businesses and products, but personally not that adventurous when it comes to ice cream. Bacon flavored ice cream is not my thang, I prefer/love my chocolate and I can get that at Dairy Queen.

If you are willing to wait in the line, you will be rewarded. I love Milk Bar. I've been to a couple of the store locations in NYC and always like to get a slice of crack pie, if I can. This recent visit to Las Vegas was no different. We had just gone for cocktails at the Chandelier Bar and Milk Bar was still open so we bee lined over for a slice of crack pie, a Thanksgiving croissant (this was new for me - turkey, stuffing, cranberry and gravy goodness, tucked in a warm croissant for $8! Perfect post-bar food) and a couple of cookies to bring back for the kids (confetti cookie and cornflake chocolate chip marshmallow cookie). Nothing is cheap, but everything was delicious and tasted just as good as it does in NYC.

Whenever I'm in Vegas, I make it a point to have breakfast every day at Bouchon bakery. It's far superior to the Wynn cafe and unsurprisingly, cheaper too! Don't bother with the drip coffee or espresso drinks here; it's like drinking water. I'm also not a fan of their madeleines--they were flavorless and foamy. But everything else I've had? Phenomenal! Try the croissants (especially the STRAWBERRY ones), Parisian macarons (coffee, vanilla, and pistachio are my favs), their muffins, the red velvet cupcake, their focaccia, and the PB&J brioche. The eponymous bouchons are just okay, but are definitely satisfying if all you want is to fulfill a chocolate-y craving.
I can't rave enough about this place. Everything is so obviously handmade because it's fan-freaking-tastic. Try anything, seriously, you won't be disappointed. It's all amazing.

My husband and I were visiting from out of town we seen that this place was a feature on Food Network (Diners, Drive Ins and Dives). In my opinion this place is severely over hyped. My Ice Cream choices were Madagascar Vanilla/Cookies & Mint which were way too sweet and the lady behind the counter wasn't very helpful considering it was our first time going. She kind of speed through the menu with no clear direction so I picked the most basic option two scoops in a cup. The location(building) is very small with cute little knick knacks other than that nothing special to me.

My most frequented place in Madison. It's legitimately embarrassing how often I end up here when I'm too lazy to cook. Delicious savory pastries. I am not one for sweets, so I'm the wrong person to evaluate their desserts; but everyone I know who has had them says they are great too. Try the gruyere and savory cream cheese croissant!

There are a variety of pastries that you can choose from. They bake it there at their bakery. All pastries are individually wrapped. You take a tray and grab whatever you want and place it on the tray. Then, you stand in line to pay for it. They also have drinks and whole cakes that you could buy as well. I got a marble taro bun, guava strudel, and a Hokkaido custard. All where amazing! The marble taro bun was very soft and chewy! On the inside there's a thick taro filling that tasted so comforting! It went so well with the bread! The guava strudel was very tasty! The guava filling was strong and the breading on the outside was very flaky, crunchy and not too sweet. I wish there was more guava filling! But, it was yummy! The Hokkaido custard was delicious! It tasted like a milk cheesecake! It was soft and creamy and the crust was baked to perfection. Soft and crunchy at the same time. I definitely would get these items again. I will be back here to try the other pastries!

Ice cream was great. Price not so much, but I guess that is what happens when you ask for homemade ice cream. I ordered 7 "Dips" of ice cream expecting a solid amount but that was not the case. No matter how I look at it, I feel gypped. It felt like just barely one scoop from the Sugar Bowl in comparison. That is my only gripe. If you are looking for great homemade ice cream this is the spot, but expect to pay for it. Sadly, I don't think I will be back but it was definitely worth a try.
too unbelievable to put into words! whatever the recipe do not ever change a thing. My mouth is watering just thinking about Jack Frost. Do you ship to Texas - lol!! 'Nuff said!

I just recently found out about Butterwood Bake Consortium and had to check it! It's essential a cake shop. The interior is rich and inviting. I love the red velvet chairs and benches. It's a pretty small space but it feels very comfortable. I almost overwhelmed by the amount of sweets options in the display case. I was also surprised to see multiple vegan options. After looking at all my options I decided to try the lemon poppy seed cake with a black berry buttercream and a hot chocolate. My two friends and I sat down and waited for desserts. The staff person was friendly and quickly brought out our cakes and drinks. The hot chocolate was a tea cup filled half way with melted chocolate that you poured cream into. It was delicious and rich! Definitely would recommend it to anyone who goes. The cake on the other hand was just okay. It was just a little to dense for liking but still a quality cake. I can't wait to go back and try more of their wonderful selections!

Had to visit the Carlos bakery and went on a sat. Night. The line was as long as a show line in Vegas. Didn't wait but went back at 745am before they opened at 8. Already 10 people in front of me. Wow but worth the wait. Very organized pleasant staff, prices reasonable, best lobster tails I ever had. The cannolis are to die for. Yum I will be back waiting in line before I leave Vegas. Kudos to the manager and to buddy.
Got donuts there this morning. Place wasn't to busy. Got a dozen donuts and they are amazing. Taste great and service was good
Just came here again. Love this place. The owner and his staff are awesome!! Love the creme brÃ»lÃ©e. I wish I could try all the different donuts. They are all amazing!

Jack Frost Donuts is your old neighborhood donut shop in Cleveland. I literally came in early one day and a police officer was having a mentoring conversation with one of the young employees. If you just sit in the parking for a while in the morning, you'll see all types of people coming in and out: the lazy grungy dude in his PJs, the businessman in a hurry, the mom with 4 kids, and multiple cops. Anyway, you'll never be disappointed eating fried cake and coffee and I wouldn't miss out on Jack's if you're looking for a Cleveland staple. My recommendations are the German Chocolate, Salted Caramel, and Maple Bacon. The coffee is self-serve and is pretty good.

Best ice cream in the city for sure, hands down, ain't no doubt about it. Due to Cleveland weather being bipolar, Mitchell's ice cream is good during the middle of a winter storm and the hottest summer day. No matter the time of year, once you have this ice cream, you'll always be craving it. Multiple creative flavors to choose from always make going feel like your first time. Okay, I'm done ranting about ice cream heaven, and I mean Mitchell's. This ice cream and its facility are just simply superb.

The best thing about Mitchells? Their vegan chocolate ice cream is literally better than any dairy-based ice cream I've ever had. Hands down. It is so creamy, velvety, and chocolatey - and all of my friends have said the same thing once I make them try it. That being said, I've also never had a bad flavor at Mitchell's. Their seasonal flavors are always on point (e.g. the coffee porter, the mint chocolate truffle, etc), and their classic flavors can't be beat (black raspberry chocolate chunk, pistachio, peanut butter, cookies and cream, bing cherry chocolate chunk, etc). Their staff are also super nice and knowledgeable about the flavors, which is fantastic when I can't decide what new flavor to try. Case in point: one day I wanted to try a new non-dairy combo, and per the staff's suggestion, I got the best smoothie I've ever had - a vegan chocolate, raspberry sorbet, and banana smoothie sent from the heavens (picture attached). When you come here, you honestly can't go wrong!

Got CRACK? I stopped by Milk Bar this evening before dinner because I enjoy my "dessert FIRST"... Awkward?! I dig the bakeries store front it's pretty hip and kind of reminds me of a food truck vibe. I ordered (2) corn cookies and (2) quakes CRACK PIE & BIRTHDAY CAKE for a total about $29 bucks. The corn cookies were amazing and full of flavor. I enjoyed the buttery cornbread tamale-like taste!Worth $3 bucks and definitely a must order. The Crack Pie Quake was sweet and delicious! Highly recommended if your a sweets junkie like myself. I was extremely disappointed in the Birthday cake quake. It was bland/flavorless I'm curious if an ingredient was skipped!! Considering the fresh products and local dairy used the pricing is decent. Regrettably, most people are use to Jack N The Box pricing which is pretty harsh to compare to an award winning pastry chefs recipes. My one gripe is it took exactly 15 minutes to prepare my two quakes with three employees on staff (I was the only person in line by the way). Two of the girls appeared very unsure of the ingredients. I witnessed a few people walking away because of the obnoxiously long wait without even being acknowledged. I'm likely to return I have a few more cookies with my name on them!!!

Ordered a small Coffee Oreo Snowstorm. I think it's a local favorite and definitely worth a try! The place is super cute and very homey, they have a lot of really interesting flavors and the service sizes are huge.

The staff is great, the doughnuts look great, and I got there at 11am...That being said I have read all the hype of this place and purchased two doughnuts...Well...I tried them and tossed them in the garbage...It is not that they are bad they are just not good...I got blueberry and meyer lemon and it had no real lemon flavor. So, one small taste and in the garbage. I tried the Butterfinger and Chocolate and one taste in the garbage. I will try it again to get more of the classic flavors. But, to date, I have tried all the doughnuts in Vegas and there are much better choices I believe.
Great place for crepes. It has been a staple of the Westside market for years!! Love going here!!

5 stars for friendly staff. 1 star for pastries. Disappointed. Cannoli was old, waxy and had funny flavor after. Bananas on the pie were old & dried. We ended up throwing everything away. because it was so bad.
So Yummy! Love the takeout containers the stickers are so cute and worth going out in the heat to grab some Ice Cream!

I have somehow managed to miss their pop up ramen nights but am so happy I caught their full time ramen menu!!!! I went with a couple of my girlfriends, two of us got the pork ramen, and another got the chicken. I got the iced tea for $7 WHICH IS ENOUGH FOR TWO TO SHARE FYI. (We didn't know it was so big but it's amazing). HOWEVER: the noodles were super fluffy but it didn't take away from the overall experience and we will still come back!
Overpriced crappy cupcakes. $4 each, 30 min wait - and you can get much better cupcakes at Walmart. These were bland & dry - don't waste your money.

My husband had heard about this ice cream shop from a coworker, and he wanted to try it out. The shop is a small older building that is located under a bridge. It has adequate parking but little seating outside. I ordered a vanilla soft-serve ice cream with peaches on top. The ice cream tasted very rich, and the peaches were sweet. I ordered a size small, but it was the perfect size for me. The employee who served us was polite. My husband ordered a root-beer float because this business seems to make their own root beer. He enjoyed his float. Prices were reasonable. We would feel happy to be return customers in the future.

New n just opened. I was excited because I have been to the Austin Texas location N loved.it. This place was small n not enough sitting place if you want to eat there. A lot of selections n price d good What turned me off is When I ordered coffee I ask for my cream which they did but charged me $3,35 for a cup no refill. Black coffee is $3.00 .And automatically add 35 cents when u asked for cream n sugar which they will add themselves. Who does that?????? I understand the no refill but cream only on my part nooooo way.
Wonderful eclairs and cream puffs, but the lobster tail pastry tasted off. Either burnt or stale or both. The filling was still delightful though.

This is pretty much the best place for hand made ice cream. If you are going there one should definitely try their dough melt. It is the best concept ever. They will put a scoop of your choice of flavor between a hot bun. The combination is OMG! This is a must try if you are in the city.

I tried this place knowing already how good their desserts are. My wife brought home a cookie and she had been dying to go back. We actually came here Before dinner this time and bought a tin of cookies. 6 for $17. We also got a slice of their crack pie and it was so good. I recommend you try that first. Next time I will try a shake or some of their soft serve concoctions. Will definitely be back. I'd give it a perfect score but it's a bit too pricey, hey, it is the strip. 4.5 stars.
Every Sprinkles is good. Oh so good. Mmmmmm. (recommend the dark chocolate, and if you want to try a ton of cupcakes, get all the minis). PLUS THERES A SPRINKLES ICE CREAM SHOP TO THE RIGHT.

The ice cream and smoothies are delicious. The only reason I rated them so long its because they have really bad customer service. The person who "helped" me out had an attitude the whole time. He acted like he was there against his will or something. I would not go back because I didn't feel welcomed at all.

I have been going to this cafe since it has been opened for almost half year. The people are kind and bubble teas are good. However, what made me happy was their coffee. Their coffee is just so good compared to other coffee (especially when u try espresso). Also, their waffles are unique too. Unlike other waffles in champaign, their waffles are really sweet without any syrup. If anyone wants to try at their shop, i recommend you to try their waffles and coffee.

I'm not sure if this place used to be better or what but we went tonight and we're so disappointed! We got the cookie ice cream cup, ice cream was flavorless and icey, macaron was hard and the marshmallow was burned. It was also 8 dollars for a single scoop of ice cream! The girl working was extremely unfriendly and service was sooo slow.
